basis: Microcephaly and intellectual disability define neurologic involvement; macrotia is a defining external-ear malformation.
Defined by skin nodules, osteochondrodystrophy and visually impairing corneal dystrophy; each occurs in 80-99%. Gingival lesions lack frequency evidence.
Structural narrowing of the gastric pylorus causes gastric outlet obstruction.
Cleft involves the oral palate; associated maxillary hypoplasia affects the facial skeleton in 30-79%.
Localized neoplasm of mature mast cells, a hematopoietic lineage; extracutaneous location alone does not establish another organ.
Squamous carcinoma originating in the bile duct; both intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Suppurative infection of the fallopian tube; the reproductive site has no anatomical axis, but the infectious mechanism does.
Acquired factor IX inhibitors cause autoimmune impairment of coagulation.
Skeletal anomalies, heart defects and intellectual disability define the syndrome; cleft lip/palate is defining GI involvement. Possible hypogonadism omitted under the four-axis cap.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising from fetal blood vessels in placental villi.
Central and peripheral neurologic disease with developmental impairment, epilepsy, ataxia and neuropathy; skeletal anomalies are each reported in under 30%.
Umbrella concept for structural malformations of the brain or spinal cord; other organ abnormalities vary by subtype.
Autonomous Leydig-cell androgen production causes precocious puberty. Accelerated skeletal maturation reflects hormonal growth effects rather than skeletal disease.
Defined as disease of the facial skeleton; additional sites in individual subtypes do not apply across the umbrella.
Defined by lipoprotein metabolism abnormalities and deafness. Atherosclerosis is a separate disease; corneal arcus does not impair ocular function.
Umbrella lipid metabolism disorder defined by deficient circulating lipoproteins; organ damage differs substantially between subtypes.
Inherited hair loss and recurrent epidermal blistering define the disease. Angular cheilitis in one assessed patient does not establish common GI involvement.
The defining triad comprises premature skull-suture fusion, intellectual disability and congenital heart defects.
Absence of urinary output represents loss of urinary-system function; classified as a kidney disorder.
Demyelinating and axonal peripheral neuropathy with developmental delay; vestibular schwannoma is also a nerve lesion. Separate ear dysfunction is not established.
Isolated sperm structural and motility defects cause male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement is described.
Dissociative identity disorder is a purely psychiatric condition; dissociative memory gaps do not establish structural neurologic disease.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation directly affects lung tissue. Reactive peripheral eosinophilia does not establish an independent blood disorder.
Senior-Loken syndrome is defined by nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration; intellectual disability occurs in 6/19 patients (~32%), just above the threshold.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and language delay occur in 30-79%. Cardiac defects and clubfoot occur in only 5-29%; facial dysmorphism adds no organ damage.
